```{r setup}
library(simttepower)
```

## What simttepower is

simttepower is a companion to
[simtte](https://github.com/csetraynor/simtte): given a trial design
(arms, a simtte model, sample size, follow-up) and a grid of scenarios
that vary one or more factors -- a model parameter, a dosing regimen, a
covariate distribution, sample size, and so on -- simttepower replicates
each scenario many times, applies one or more analysis functions to
each simulated trial, and summarises operating characteristics (power,
type I error) across the grid. It runs that replication sequentially,
across local worker processes, or split into independent chunks for a
job scheduler -- all three give byte-identical results for the same
seed, which is this vignette's own running theme.

## Building blocks: `arm()` and `trial_design()`

An `arm()` is everything [simtte::sim_tte_ode()] needs to simulate one
trial arm, plus a label. A `trial_design()` collects one or more arms
and the analysis function(s) applied to their simulated events:

```{r design}
p <- list(CL = 2, V2 = 20, KA = 1, KIN = 1, KOUT = 0.5, IC50 = 1,
  IMAX = 0.9, H0 = 0.15)

comparator <- arm(label = "comparator", n = 20, model = "irm1_hazard",
  end = 24, param = p)
experimental <- arm(label = "experimental", n = 20, model = "irm1_hazard",
  end = 24, param = p)

design <- trial_design(
  arms = list(comparator, experimental),
  analyses = list(coxph = analysis_coxph)
)
```

## A grid of scenarios: `scenario_grid()`

`regimen` is a label, never derived automatically from a dosing data
frame -- a loading-then-maintenance schedule has no single meaningful
numeric summary. Here the experimental arm's `data` (its dosing events)
is the varied factor, contrasting once-weekly dosing against a
loading-then-maintenance schedule:

```{r grid}
qw <- data.frame(ID = 1:20, time = 0, amt = 100, cmt = 1, evid = 1,
  ii = 1, addl = 23)                                    # 100, once weekly
q4w_loading <- data.frame(ID = 1:20, time = 0, amt = 400, cmt = 1,
  evid = 1, ii = 4, addl = 5)                            # 400 q4w x 6 doses

dosing_arm <- arm(label = "experimental", n = 20, model = "irm1_hazard",
  end = 24, param = p, data = qw, regimen = "qw")

design_dosing <- trial_design(
  arms = list(comparator, dosing_arm),
  analyses = list(coxph = function(events) {
    analysis_coxph(events, formula = ~ regimen)
  })
)

grid <- scenario_grid(design_dosing, over = list(
  arm = "experimental", field = "data", values = list(qw, q4w_loading)))
grid
```

## Running the replication engine: `power_sim()`

`power_sim(grid, n_sims, seed)` simulates and analyses every
(scenario x replicate) combination, sequentially by default:

```{r power_sim}
res <- power_sim(grid, n_sims = 8, seed = 1, progress = FALSE)
res
```

`power_sim(seed = s)` run twice gives byte-identical `results`
(excluding `runtime_sec`, real wall-clock time) -- the same seed always
gives the same answer, regardless of how the run is later parallelised
or chunked (the rest of this vignette).

## `summary()` and `plot_power()`

`summary()` collapses the raw per-replicate results to one row per
(scenario x analysis): rejection rate (power, here, since the two arms'
`param` differ only in dosing, not in the underlying hazard), its
binomial SE, error counts, and median event/runtime summaries.

```{r summary}
summary(res)
```

`plot_power()` plots a rejection-rate curve over one varied factor from
that summary -- here with a plain factor column, since `data` (the
varied field in this example) isn't itself a plottable x-axis; a
numeric varied factor (a sample size or parameter grid) plots directly.
Requires `ggplot2` (`Suggests`); skipped below if it isn't installed.

```{r plot, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
grid_n <- scenario_grid(design, over = list(arm = "experimental",
  field = "n", values = c(20, 40, 60)))
res_n <- power_sim(grid_n, n_sims = 8, seed = 2, progress = FALSE)
plot_power(summary(res_n), x = "n")
```

## Running on multiple local workers

`power_sim(..., workers = 2)` dispatches across local worker processes
(`parallel::parLapply()` by default, or `parallel::mclapply()` on Unix
via `parallel = "fork"`) instead of running sequentially --
`power_sim(seed = s, workers = 1)` and `workers = 2` give byte-identical
`results`. Under the hood, `power_sim()` calls
`simtte::simtte_prepare_model()` (see `?simtte::simtte_prepare_model`)
once per distinct model, in this process, before any worker starts --
every worker then only ever loads that already-compiled model, never
rebuilds it.

```{r parallel, eval = parallel::detectCores() >= 2}
res_parallel <- power_sim(grid, n_sims = 8, seed = 1, progress = FALSE,
  workers = 2)
identical(res$results[setdiff(names(res$results), "runtime_sec")],
  res_parallel$results[setdiff(names(res_parallel$results), "runtime_sec")])
```

## Chunking a run for a cluster

For a run too large for one machine's local workers, `power_sim_chunks()`/
`power_sim_chunk()`/`power_sim_merge()` split it into independent chunks
that can execute as separate processes -- on a job scheduler (SGE,
Slurm; see the array-job templates and README under
`system.file("templates", package = "simttepower")`), or, as shown here,
just in a loop on one machine. No scheduler dependency: plain files (a
manifest plus one file per chunk) are the entire mechanism, and the
result is byte-identical to a single sequential `power_sim()` call
regardless of how many chunks it was split into:

```{r chunks}
chunk_dir <- tempfile()
power_sim_chunks(grid, n_sims = 8, seed = 1, n_chunks = 2, dir = chunk_dir)
for (i in 1:2) power_sim_chunk(chunk_dir, i, progress = FALSE)
res_chunked <- power_sim_merge(chunk_dir)

identical(res$results[setdiff(names(res$results), "runtime_sec")],
  res_chunked$results[setdiff(names(res_chunked$results), "runtime_sec")])
```

Each array-job task in the templates calls `power_sim_chunk(dir, i)`
where `i` only ever selects *which rows of the manifest* that task
owns -- the seed lives once, on the manifest `power_sim_chunks()`
wrote, never derived from a task id.

## The estimand boundary

Simulation-side parameters -- a `param` entry, a dose, a covariate
distribution -- are *truth*, baked into a scenario; they are never
something an analysis function estimates. Power here is always about a
contrast or coefficient an analysis function estimates from the
simulated `events` and the labels `power_sim()` attaches to them
(`arm`, `regimen`, `dose` when declared, and any `covariates` columns):
between arms, across dose levels, or adjusted for covariates.
Estimating a nonlinear PK/PD parameter (an `IC50`, an `EMAX`) from event
data is out of scope -- bring your own analysis function for that.

## Other patterns

A few capabilities not walked through step by step above, each covered
in its own reference page:

- **Covariate-adjusted analysis**: `arm(covariates = , beta = )` joins a
  covariate data frame onto simulated events at baseline; any analysis
  function's own `formula` can then include it (`?arm`, `?analysis_coxph`).
- **Interval-censored events**: an analysis function is any
  `function(events, ...) -> named numeric`, so a fit on
  [simtte::add_interval_censoring()]'s output needs no separate
  simttepower code path -- just a user-supplied analysis function
  calling `survival::Surv(..., type = "interval2")`.
- **Direction-aware rejection**: [reject_direction()] additionally
  requires a rejection's sign to match a scenario's declared `truth`
  (`scenario_grid(truth = )`), rather than [reject_default()]'s plain
  `p < alpha`.
